proposed_widenings.name: magic_item_ongoing_hazard_component
proposed_widenings.justification: The item has a persistent triggered hazard that damages specific creature types on touch and again on turn end while they continue carrying it. Current magic-item mechanics only allow passive grants, activated abilities, and triggered reactions.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A Fiend or an Undead that touches the talisman takes 8d6 Radiant damage and takes the damage again each time it ends its turn holding or carrying the talisman.

proposed_widenings.name: destroy_target
proposed_widenings.justification: Pure Rebuke's failed-save outcome is deterministic creature removal with no remains, not damage, condition application, transport, or any existing effect atom.
proposed_widenings.evidence: On a failed save, the target falls into the fissure and is destroyed, leaving no remains.

proposed_widenings.name: save_gate.disadvantage_for_target_types
proposed_widenings.justification: The save gate needs a target-side creature-type conditional disadvantage rider. Existing target type filters gate who can be selected, and existing roll-advantage filters cover attacker-side roll modifiers, not the target's save within a save gate.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If the target is a Fiend or an Undead, it has Disadvantage on the save.

proposed_widenings.name: grounded_target_restriction
proposed_widenings.justification: Pure Rebuke only targets a creature on the ground. Current targeting grammar can express range and creature-type filters, but not positional state like grounded versus airborne.
proposed_widenings.evidence: target one creature you can see on the ground within 120 feet of yourself

proposed_widenings.name: spell_attack_only_roll_modifier
proposed_widenings.justification: The passive holy-symbol bonus applies only to spell attack rolls. The current roll-modifier surface only offers generic attack-roll targeting, which would incorrectly also buff weapon attacks.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls while you wear or hold it.

notes: Existing composite magic-item mechanics can represent the attunement restriction, a held-or-worn activation gate, the charge pool, Magic action cost, last-charge destruction, and the successful-save psychic damage rider. The item still does not fit honestly because its passive contact hazard requires a missing non-reaction triggered component family, the holy-symbol rider needs spell-attack-only roll scoping, and the activated fissure's failed-save outcome requires a missing destroy-creature atom.
